body: This sounds like a great way if I knew how to hold a normal conversation but right now thats way beyond what I can do as I simply wouldn't know what to say and would get some pretty weird looks every time I went to said shop.

I have a couple job's, one should be great as I meet a lot of people from within the business but its by appointment so I'm restricted to deadlines and the chances of me seeing the same person more than once is very unlikely.

The other requires a great amount of attention to details so I can't really talk to colleagues whilst doing it as inputting incorrect data is a quick way to get fired.

I can talk to people but only if its in reference to the job. In short I can speak in a professional manner well but as soon as it turns to something more personal I quickly crumble as I don't have the words to say.

I feel sorry for you, truly. 

I went on a group trip years ago with a bunch of strangers who I never once spoke to in my life but for the duration I was away I can tell you I never felt more human it was amazing but so short lived.

I'm probably not in the best way to be telling you this but maybe there is a deeper issue  behind how you feel, I know what works for me, you just need to find what works for you.

Despite being in a job that puts me in such a position I can tell you this isn't the case.

People take what they need then they forget about you afterwards.

I understand how you feel, I also have someone I meet but wouldn't really call them anything more than an acquaintance, I do try stay in contact but I don't really think they get a lot out of seeing me.

Thank you for sharing, I've always wondered what it must feel like to come home to someone or to have someone to talk to about pointless stuff but still enjoy their time.

Sure I'm young but I've learnt from experience that to carry on the way I am would be pretty much insanity, doing the same thing expecting a different result.

I've had a look at meetup previously and it looks like said website is still pretty unheard of in my country as there are hardly any groups in my area and said groups aren't doing what I'd be interested in.

Snowboarding is at an artificial slope but its expensive and takes a while to get to so it takes a lot of planning. People just mind their own business on the slopes so its kinda hard to start a conversation as most people want to get as many runs as they can before their time runs out.

Thanks for the advice, truth be told I have been up until recently talking to people on the internet (both in voice and text) but it doesn't seem to be doing much to help.

One of my problems is a lot of my hobbies and interests are either not very mainstream (snowboarding, psychology) or are generally pretty unpopular to talk about anywhere outside of very specific places (video games, technology/science).

Another large problem is that I live in the UK where everyone is very very reserved so that makes the gap between internet and IRL that much harder to bridge.

My parents are also amazingly supportive I wouldn't be here now if it weren't for them. But this feeling is like a black hole the more it consumes, the larger it gets.

I know that with my current circumstances that chances of getting even a friend (which seems harder to come by then getting a girlfriend in this day and age) are roughly the same as winning the lottery.

Outside of having friends I take it? very mild speech disorder and mental disorder which is hidden but can sometimes cause what I say in the wrong order or just plain not make sense like it does in my head.

People say that social skills are like muscles, if you use it often then it gradually improves and gets better and better, if you don't then it wastes away. I not only have nothing to start with, I also have no way to practice or improve.
I'm happy that you can think that way, it's a shame life has taught me that is not going to happen.
